run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:23:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because the proxy returns error responses on live user traffic and its own spans carry ERROR status. In 17:28–17:40 its Envoy access log shows 453 lines matching "500 - via_upstream" (repeatedly on GET /api/data?contextKeys=...) plus 11 "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" lines. The 500s are the frontend's responses, not a proxy fault: frontend's error spans on GET, "GET /api/data", "executing api route (pages) /api/data" and "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" are all exactly 503.48 per 20m, so each failing /api/data request corresponds to a failing GetAds call. The deepest failing entity is the ad service: its own server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carries 473.6 error spans per 20m out of ~702.8 total (~67%), and its pod logs one "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed" line per failing call. Ad's error spans are fast (median 1.33 ms, p90 88 ms) while its successful calls slowed from a 1.41 ms median at 17:25 to 137.5 ms at 17:47, its container CPU rose from ~0.006 to ~0.0165 cores with a flat GetAds call rate (0.85–1.1 spans/s), JVM CPU utilization went 0.28→0.54–0.70, and its CFS throttling rose from 10–18% to 34–48% of periods against its 50m CPU limit. Node saturation, frontend throttling and a proxy-internal fault were each checked and are not supported. What made the ad handler start throwing is not resolvable with the available data (flagd runtime flag state is not observable and trace detail ends at ~17:08); that remains an open hypothesis.

claims.text: frontend-proxy (service_name=frontend-proxy) shows a rising STATUS_CODE_ERROR span count: 15.2 per 25m at 17:29:53, 104.1 at 17:30:53, then 294, 489, 708, 928 and a plateau of ~1012–1022 per 25m by 17:42–17:47, while its STATUS_CODE_UNSET span rate stayed roughly flat (~24.8k–35.1k per 25m).

frontend-proxy's own access log for 17:28:00–17:40:00 contains 453 lines matching "500 - via_upstream", e.g. "GET /api/data?contextKeys=assembly HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream ... frontend 100.96.3.229:39358 100.96.3.229:8080 100.96.2.96:37922, i.e. the proxy received the response from the frontend upstream rather than failing to connect.

frontend-proxy also logged 11 lines with "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" in the same 17:28–17:40 window (e.g. GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP → 503 UC), so a small minority of its errors are the frontend terminating connections before response start.

At 17:47:00 the per-operation error increases over 20m are: frontend span_name GET 503.48, frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 503.48, frontend "GET /api/data" 503.48 and "executing api route (pages) /api/data" 503.48; ad span_name oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 473.60; frontend-proxy ingress 518.24 and "router frontend egress" 504.66; frontend cart/checkout calls, payment and accounting operations 0.

ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans in the same 20m window: 473.60 STATUS_CODE_ERROR vs 229.23 STATUS_CODE_UNSET (about 67% of ~702.8 spans erroring); frontend's client-side grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans: 503.48 ERROR vs 240.75 UNSET, i.e. the caller and the ad server agree on the failure.

ad's error spans are short: median 1.33 ms and p90 88.1 ms for STATUS_CODE_ERROR, versus median 137.5 ms and p90 520 ms for its STATUS_CODE_UNSET (non-error) spans, so the failing GetAds calls are immediate failures rather than client deadline timeouts.
ad's median latency for non-error GetAds spans was 1.41 ms at 17:25:00 (before the surge) and 137.5 ms at 17:47:00, a roughly 100x increase for the calls that still succeed.

Pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg (owner ReplicaSet ad-554b849958, owner Deployment ad) repeatedly logs "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@..." — 301 matching lines in 17:29–17:36 and continuous occurrences through 17:37–17:38 — interleaved with its normal per-request lines "no baggage found in context" and "Targeted ad request received for [...]", i.e. an uncaught exception on the GetAds server call path; the lines carry no stack-trace text.

The ad container's CFS throttling ratio rose from 0.098–0.181 (17:06:53–17:28:53) to 0.340, 0.453, 0.468, 0.389, 0.407, 0.409 and 0.476 at 17:30:53–17:42:53, so it began exhausting its CPU quota as the GetAds errors began; the Deployment sets the ad container cpu limit to 50m (request 10m).

ad's own CPU demand rose with a flat call rate: container cpu usage went from ~0.0060–0.0084 cores (17:07–17:29) to 0.0119, 0.0159, 0.0165, 0.0140, 0.0143 cores at 17:31–17:39, while its GetAds span rate stayed flat at ~0.85–1.12 spans/s, and its JVM jvm_cpu_recent_utilization_ratio rose from 0.24–0.42 to 0.46–0.70 with heap (G1 Old Gen ~29–33 MB) unchanged.

The ad pod was not restarted or evicted during the window: ad-554b849958-sk6fg is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, state running since 2026-11-16T16:53:40Z, empty lastState, owned by ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 (created 16:53:37Z) which is controlled by Deployment ad; a query for Kubernetes events referencing ad pods returned no objects.
Every otel-demo pod was Running and Ready with restartCount 0 at query time (21 pods, including ad, frontend, frontend-proxy and flagd), so no workload was down at pod level.

Node-level saturation is not the cause: ad, frontend and frontend-proxy all run on node i-00919402a8ea35027, whose summed container CPU usage stayed ~0.184–0.207 cores out of 4 allocatable throughout (no rise at 17:30), and all five nodes report Ready with no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure.

frontend CPU throttling as the cause is rejected: the frontend container's throttling ratio was already 0.324–0.382 for every sample from 16:30 to 17:41 (no change at onset) and its cpu usage stayed flat at ~0.055–0.058 cores, so it cannot explain a change that began at ~17:30:53.

A fault inside frontend-proxy is not supported: its container CPU is flat (~0.014–0.016 cores), its throttling ratio never exceeded 0.3, and its failing requests are logged as upstream responses ("500 - via_upstream" from frontend) plus only 11 upstream-reset 503s, so it reports its upstream's failures rather than generating its own.
Traffic did not increase: frontend-proxy ingress span rate stayed ~10.1–13.1 spans/s and frontend GET span rate ~4.7–10.0 spans/s across 16:30–17:43, so the error surge is not load-driven.

A baseline failure existed before the surge: a sampled frontend-proxy trace at 17:06:37 shows an "ingress" server span with error=true/http.status_code=503 and a child "router frontend egress" client span with error=true/http.status_code=0 (no upstream status), and the frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase was already ~12 spans per 25m at 17:20:53.

The ad GetAds handler is failing on a fault-injection/feature-flag code path: flagd-config defines flags "adFailure" ("Fail ad service"), "adHighCpu" ("Triggers high cpu load in the ad service") and "adManualGc", and ad's simultaneous shape — immediate 1.3 ms error spans, per-request uncaught handler exceptions, ~2.5x CPU per call with flat traffic — is consistent with injected failure plus CPU load. This remains a hypothesis: the ConfigMap shows defaultVariant "off" for all flags at query time, which does not prove what flagd served at ~17:30, and flagd runtime state is not observable with the available tools.

The ad container's 50m CPU limit contributes degradation but is not the error mechanism: throttling rose to 34–48% of periods and successful GetAds latency grew from 1.41 ms to 137.5 ms (p90 520 ms) after onset, consistent with quota-induced queueing, but the failing calls return in ~1.3 ms, which quota throttling does not explain.

A broken flagd dependency for ad is possible but unproven: ad carries an error span on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (starting 17:00:13, 594 s duration), yet the same stream error appears at low baseline rates for fraud-detection and recommendation (~1–3 per 20m) with no new errors on their own operations, and the ad span pre-dates the 17:30:53 surge.

Services checked and not showing their own new failures: payment and accounting returned 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans over the last 20m; frontend cart/checkout AddItem/GetCart/PlaceOrder and the cart and checkout API routes are 0; recommendation and fraud-detection carry only their usual flagd EventStream noise (1.05 and 2.09 per 20m). No STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned at all for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote or shipping, which is not proof that they had zero errors.

Read the live flagd flag state (e.g. via flagd's flag/OfRep API) for adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc as of the incident, and obtain the ad service exception class and stack trace (enable stack-trace logging or capture a thread dump), before attributing the handler exceptions to a specific trigger.

If the ad latency degradation matters beyond the fast failures, review the ad container's 50m CPU limit against observed demand (~0.0165 cores average with 34–48% of CFS periods throttled); the limit is configured on Deployment ad in namespace otel-demo.

gaps: Jaeger returned no traces for frontend after 17:08 (empty result for 17:40–17:47, and the sampled traces stop at 17:07:59), so span status codes, tags and parent links for the actual 17:30+ error surge could not be inspected; the per-operation failure attribution for the surge rests on spanmetrics series, not on trace detail.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules, status no_data), so the rule expression, window and denominator — and therefore the annotation value "current: 2.1111111111111107" — could not be verified; observed frontend-proxy error counts around 17:20–17:23 (~12 error spans per 25m against ~12.5 ingress spans/s) are far below that figure.

The queries for rpc_server/http_server metric names and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series (status no_data), so gRPC-level status-code and latency counters independent of spanmetrics were unavailable; only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket exist for these services.

A throttling query grouped by pod label and a trace search for frontend error=true traces in 17:00–17:08 and 17:40–17:47 returned no data, so pod-label-grouped throttling and frontend trace detail in those slices are unknown rather than zero.

flagd runtime flag state is not observable with the available tools (no flagd metrics in Prometheus and no flagd API tool); the flagd-config ConfigMap only shows flag definitions with defaultVariant "off" at query time, so whether adFailure/adHighCpu/adManualGc was enabled at ~17:30 is unverified.
The ad pod's exception log lines contain no stack-trace text, so the thrown exception class/message and the exact failing code path inside getAds are unknown.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 17:28–17:36 (0 lines read, status no_data), so frontend-side error text for the failing /api/data route is unknown.
The change_history integration is not available, so configuration changes (including the ad Deployment's CPU limit) cannot be correlated with the incident timeline.
next_steps: Check the live and historical flagd flag values for adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc at ~17:30 UTC to confirm or rule out the feature-flag fault-injection hypothesis for the ad service.
Capture the ad service exception type and stack trace for the GetAds server-stream failures (enable stack-trace logging or take a thread dump) to identify the exact failing code path.

Review the ad Deployment's 50m CPU limit and 10m request against observed per-call CPU growth and 34–48% CFS throttling, since throttling is degrading successful GetAds latency even if it does not cause the fast failures.

Verify the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the alerting Prometheus (it is not visible in this data source) to confirm the metric, threshold and window behind the reported value 2.1111111111111107.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
